hunks.baseline: A complete ruin. There was no need to add or subtract a single word.
hunks.sol: A complete ruin. No other words were needed.

hunks.baseline: But the man who had appeared in a sudden flash of light barely ten seconds ago saw it a little differently.
hunks.sol: But the man who had appeared in a sudden flash of light barely ten seconds ago saw it differently.

hunks.baseline: He could feel it the moment he looked around—or even before he opened his eyes. The aura of death swallowing everything around him like a thick fog at dawn. The screams of countless vengeful spirits rising from every corner of this enormous grave, where not a ray of light could penetrate the clouds overhead.
hunks.sol: He could feel it the moment he looked around—no, even before he opened his eyes. Death saturated the air like thick fog at dawn. From every corner of this enormous grave, where the clouds overhead shut out every ray of light, rose the screams of countless vengeful spirits.

hunks.baseline: “……I suppose so.”
hunks.sol: “…Of course.”

hunks.baseline: “Fine. I’ll go there.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. I’m going there.”

hunks.baseline: “If that’s what you really want…… Fine, I’ll allow it. There’s no harm in keeping you company for a little while.”
hunks.sol: “If that’s what you really want… Fine, I’ll allow it. Having you along for a little while wouldn’t be so bad.”

hunks.baseline: First, by the man’s behavior, which made him look insane.
hunks.sol: First, the man was behaving like a lunatic.

hunks.baseline: And second, by the fact that this madman was famous all over the world.
hunks.sol: Second, this lunatic was someone the whole world knew.

hunks.baseline: They were certainly different kinds of beings, but they were linked by the word *death*.
hunks.sol: They were different kinds of beings, certainly, but death linked them.

hunks.baseline: The man continued, as if talking to himself.
hunks.sol: The man went on as if talking to himself.

hunks.baseline: “That’s impossible. You did nothing wrong. It was just a simple misfortune. Something that can happen to anyone.”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. You did nothing wrong. It was just a misfortune, the kind that could happen to anyone.”

hunks.baseline: “……Your child, huh? I see. But don’t worry. A child that young would have gone to heaven. No—they definitely did.”
hunks.sol: “…Your child, huh? I see. But don’t worry. A child that young would have gone to heaven. No, I’m sure of it.”

hunks.baseline: “You there. Take that back. I’m a great being, far beyond the likes of you. My memory’s just a little bad, that’s all.”
hunks.sol: “You there. Take that back. I am a great being, far beyond the likes of you. My memory’s just a little bad, that’s all.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve given it some serious thought, and I think I must have been human once, too. An incredibly noble and excellent human, just like I am now—damn it. Everyone, quiet down. I’m having an important conversation.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve given it some serious thought, and I think I must have been human once, too. An incredibly noble and admirable human, just like I am now—damn it. Everyone, quiet down. I’m trying to say something important.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, don’t cry. I wasn’t talking to you. How old are you? What about your parents?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, don’t cry. I wasn’t talking to you. How old are you? Where are your parents?”

hunks.baseline: “……All right. I can’t promise, but if I find your parents, I’ll make sure you see them.”
hunks.sol: “…All right. I can’t promise anything, but if I find your parents, I’ll make sure you see them.”

hunks.baseline: The man continued forward, carrying on his conversation with the spirits.
hunks.sol: The man continued forward, talking with the spirits as he went.

hunks.baseline: A young man who had only just taken his first steps into adulthood. An old man who had accepted his own death and asked about the afterlife. Parents who had lost a child, and a child who had lost their parents.
hunks.sol: A young man who had only just taken his first steps into adulthood. An old man who had accepted his death and wanted to know about the afterlife. Parents who had lost a child, and a child who had lost their parents.

hunks.baseline: The scenery changed in an instant, but the spirits never stopped whispering. They were indignant and furious at the death that had struck without warning, grieving even as they trembled with fear.
hunks.sol: The scenery flew past, and the spirits never stopped whispering. They were angry at the death that had struck without warning, grieving and afraid.

hunks.baseline: Because he was their king.
hunks.sol: Because he was a king.

hunks.baseline: The only being with the right and duty to guide those who had lost everything in an instant and now wandered the Nine Springs—those who had become his people.
hunks.sol: He alone had the right and the duty to guide those who had lost everything in an instant and now wandered the Nine Springs—those who had become his people.

hunks.baseline: But perhaps the spirits weren’t the only ones finding comfort and peace in this strange conversation.
hunks.sol: But perhaps the spirits weren’t the only ones finding comfort in this strange conversation.

hunks.baseline: “Why did I come here? Hmm, that’s an excellent question. This is an epic tale that begins with the most handsome and excellent hero in the world.”
hunks.sol: “Why did I come here? Hmm, excellent question. This is an epic tale that begins with the most handsome and admirable hero in the world.”

hunks.baseline: “The hero had many talents. He was incredibly strong and had a noble heart. But for all his abilities, he was surrounded by idiots and incompetents. Then one day, he learned that the biggest fool of them all had gotten himself into trouble.”
hunks.sol: “The hero had many talents. He was incredibly strong and had a noble heart. But despite all that, he was surrounded by idiots and incompetents. Then one day, he learned that the biggest fool of them all was in trouble.”

hunks.baseline: “While the hero was deep in thought, some ignorant bastard who was crazy about booze and cigarettes told him that people see what they want to see and believe what they want to believe. So the hero decided to borrow the fool’s appearance for a while.”
hunks.sol: “While the hero was deep in thought, an ignorant bastard who loved booze and cigarettes told him that people see what they want to see and believe what they want to believe. So the hero decided to borrow the fool’s appearance for a while.”

hunks.baseline: “Actually, I didn’t know I had that ability. No, neither did the hero. But when he tried it, it worked. It wasn’t nearly as good as the Doppelganger’s original ability, though.”
hunks.sol: “Actually, I didn’t know I could do that. No, the hero didn’t. But when he tried it, it worked. It wasn’t nearly as good as the Doppelganger’s own ability, though.”

hunks.baseline: Was it because of his innate ability to grow stronger by absorbing the magical power of monsters that had been destroyed? Or was it because his magical power levels had already reached the point of going berserk?
hunks.sol: Was it thanks to the ability that had let him grow stronger by absorbing the magical power of destroyed monsters? Or was it because his magical power had already reached the point of going berserk?

hunks.baseline: Amazingly, the hero, who wasn’t human, had gained a new power he’d never discovered before. After traveling thousands of kilometers by way of several Warp Gates, he had made it here.
hunks.sol: Amazingly, the hero, who wasn’t human, had discovered a new power. After changing Warp Gates several times and traveling thousands of kilometers, he had made it here.

hunks.baseline: Of course, there had been some trouble along the way.
hunks.sol: Of course, there had been a little trouble along the way.

hunks.baseline: He’d threatened the mages who refused to activate the Warp Gate. Or he’d taken a selfie in his current appearance, posted it on social media, and deliberately spread the word far and wide.
hunks.sol: He’d threatened mages who refused to activate a Warp Gate. He’d also posted a selfie of his current appearance on social media and deliberately spread the word far and wide.

hunks.baseline: The grand finale—the most important part of this story—was still to come.
hunks.sol: The crowning touch of his story was still to come.

hunks.baseline: In the sudden silence, the man blinked after making his solemn declaration.
hunks.sol: Silence fell. The man blinked, his solemn declaration still hanging in the air.

hunks.baseline: “Why is everyone so quiet? You’d think you were dead. Oh, right. You are dead.”
hunks.sol: “Why is everyone so quiet? You’d think someone had died. No, wait. You’re already dead.”

hunks.baseline: “What? You didn’t see it coming? That’s impossible. The foreshadowing was perfect from the start. I said I was the most handsome and excellent man in the world—damn it. Forget it. You stupid humans.”
hunks.sol: “What? You didn’t see it coming? Impossible. I planted the clues perfectly from the start. I said he was the most handsome and admirable—damn it. Forget it. Stupid humans.”

hunks.baseline: That was when the grumbling man suddenly stopped walking.
hunks.sol: That was when he stopped walking.

hunks.baseline: “……I’m already here.”
hunks.sol: “…I’m here already?”

hunks.baseline: He murmured and looked at the scenery, now completely transformed.
hunks.sol: He murmured and looked at the changed scenery.

hunks.baseline: As if someone had drawn a line dividing the world, a pitch-black landscape lay only a few steps ahead, starkly different from everything behind him.
hunks.sol: As if someone had drawn a line across the world, pitch-black earth lay only a few steps ahead, starkly different from the ground behind him.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, the countless spirits surrounding him let out their screams.
hunks.sol: At the same time, the countless spirits surrounding him began to scream.

hunks.baseline: Screams filled with a terror unlike anything they had shown before.
hunks.sol: Their cries were filled with a terror unlike anything he’d heard from them before.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t be so afraid. Weak spirits like you would have a hard time entering that place anyway. Not that I was planning to take you with me in the first place.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t be so afraid. Weak spirits like you would have a hard time entering that place anyway. Not that I was planning to take you with me.”

hunks.baseline: The spirits writhed as if burned by fire, but he knew that the closer he got to that ominous, pitch-black landscape, the stronger he would become.
hunks.sol: While the spirits writhed as if burned by fire, he knew he would grow stronger the closer he came to that ominous, pitch-black earth.

hunks.baseline: *In the end, only appearances can be faked.*
hunks.sol: *After all, the only thing I can fake is my appearance.*

hunks.baseline: As the words echoed emptily in his mind, the man drew the sword tucked at his waist.
hunks.sol: The thought faded hollowly in his mind as he drew the sword tucked at his waist.

hunks.baseline: Its blade was clear as untainted ice.
hunks.sol: Its blade was clear as ice without a trace of impurity.

hunks.baseline: The man silently gazed at his reflection in it.
hunks.sol: The man silently gazed at his reflection.

hunks.baseline: Or rather, at the face of the person who was probably chasing him as fast as he could somewhere out there.
hunks.sol: Or rather, at the face of someone who must be somewhere out there right now, doing his best to catch up.

hunks.baseline: The man—the Skeleton King—snickered. Someone reflected in the blade snickered along with him.
hunks.sol: The man—the Skeleton King—snickered. The person reflected in the blade smiled along with him.

hunks.baseline: That fool—that Jin Taekyung—deserved to smile.
hunks.sol: That fool—Jin Taekyung—deserved to smile.

hunks.baseline: “Then, here I go.”
hunks.sol: “Well, here I go.”

hunks.baseline: With a final farewell that would never reach him, the Skeleton King took a firm step forward.
hunks.sol: With a final farewell that would never reach him, the Skeleton King stepped forward.

hunks.baseline: Using the light spilling from his sword as a torch, he headed for the land of death, where magical power churned, and thought:
hunks.sol: Using the light spilling from his sword as a torch, he headed into the land of death, where magical power churned.

hunks.baseline: After he met his glorious end in the form of Jin Taekyung—not the Skeleton King or the Stone King—all of humanity would understand.
hunks.sol: Once he met a glorious end in the form of Jin Taekyung—not the Skeleton King or the Stone King—all of humanity would understand.

hunks.baseline: They would understand how foolish they had been to believe the monsters’ promise to stop the destruction and slaughter if they handed over Jin Taekyung.
hunks.sol: They would see how foolish they had been to believe the monster’s promise to stop the destruction and slaughter if they handed over Jin Taekyung.

hunks.baseline: And they would understand the only way to escape this catastrophe.
hunks.sol: And they would see the only way out of this catastrophe.

hunks.baseline: The dense fog drifting over the pitch-black land swallowed his retreating figure.
hunks.sol: The dense fog drifting over the pitch-black earth swallowed his retreating figure.

hunks.baseline: Morgoth recalled an old saying he’d heard long ago: Sometimes, a certain kind of curiosity can shorten a person’s life.
hunks.sol: Morgoth recalled a saying he’d heard long ago: Certain kinds of curiosity could shorten a person’s life.

hunks.baseline: Unlike humans, the Dragon race couldn’t live long without curiosity. Morgoth himself was the perfect example.
hunks.sol: Unlike humans, Dragons couldn’t live long without curiosity. Morgoth himself was a prime example.

hunks.baseline: Ever since he was no more than a Hatchling—or even before he broke out of his egg.
hunks.sol: Ever since he was no more than a Hatchling—before he’d even broken out of his egg.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps that was why Morgoth had become a being unlike any other Dragon.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why Morgoth had become unlike other Dragons.

hunks.baseline: Nothing short of the very best could satisfy his curiosity.
hunks.sol: His curiosity would not rest until he had reached the highest level of whatever caught his interest.

hunks.baseline: Humans, of course, but also Dwarves, Elves, and all sorts of other races. Driven by nothing but curiosity, he had spent unfathomable stretches of time among them, learning from them and giving in turn, while also ruling over them.
hunks.sol: Humans, Dwarves, Elves, and other races besides—driven solely by curiosity, he had spent ages among them, learning and giving in turn, and ruling over them as well.

hunks.baseline: No matter how often he changed his appearance or location, Morgoth was a born ruler.
hunks.sol: No matter how often he changed his appearance or where he went, Morgoth was a born ruler.

hunks.baseline: His election as Dragon Lord before he had even lived a thousand years was proof of that.
hunks.sol: His election as Dragon Lord before he was even a thousand years old was proof.

hunks.baseline: At least, he would have been, if not for the one curiosity he had never been able to satisfy.
hunks.sol: Or he would have been, if not for the one question he had never answered.

hunks.baseline: The home of all monsters. The land of demons, where poison, corpses, and death flowed in place of clear rivers.
hunks.sol: The home of all monsters. A land of demons where poison, corpses, and death flowed instead of clear river water.

hunks.baseline: But why? Even after an extraordinarily long time had passed, the curiosity filling Morgoth’s heart had not faded.
hunks.sol: But why? Even after an extraordinarily long time, the curiosity filling Morgoth’s heart had not faded.

hunks.baseline: And among his unanswered questions was one that, like the saying among humans, might truly shorten his life.
hunks.sol: And among his unanswered questions was one that, as the human saying went, might truly shorten his life.

hunks.baseline: Morgoth possessed immeasurable knowledge and power, but he didn’t know why he had come to this world.
hunks.sol: Morgoth possessed knowledge and power beyond measure, yet he did not know why he had come to this world.

hunks.baseline: He had simply been summoned from beyond distant stars and space, and answered the call.
hunks.sol: One day, a call had reached him from beyond those distant stars and the space between them, and he had answered it. That was all.

hunks.baseline: That made it all the harder to understand.
hunks.sol: Which made it even harder to understand.

hunks.baseline: Unlike the others, he was not devoted to serving Demon King Asmodeus, nor did he intend to give his life for him.
hunks.sol: Unlike the others, he was neither devoted to serving Demon King Asmodeus nor willing to give his life for him.

hunks.baseline: *Besides, how could you, a being who doesn’t exist in this world, have prepared a stage like this?*
hunks.sol: *Besides, how could you, when you don’t even exist in this world, have prepared a stage like this?*

hunks.baseline: But Morgoth did not delve deeply into these questions.
hunks.sol: But Morgoth did not pursue these questions further.

hunks.baseline: No. To be precise, he had to put them aside for now.
hunks.sol: No. More precisely, he had to set them aside for now.

hunks.baseline: The guest he had truly wanted to meet had just arrived at his palace.
hunks.sol: The guest he had so wanted to meet had just arrived at his palace.
